x: Also on the programme were a few junior events and Walton again proved successful in these by scoring 27 points to our 18 and Ealing's 10. George Stace ran well in the mile, and Brian Rice ran second in the half mile. Dave Marshall won the 220 yards in fine style in 23.8.
The 880 yds. saw Brian Rice making a welcome appearance in our colours and with Harry Greene they managed to finish 3rd and 4th, although we actually had two non-scorers in Doug.
Godfrey second and Brian Rice third.
Brian Rice our young Junior half-miler has now been called-up and sends his best wishes to his many friends in the club. Percy Wright has now added a daughter to his family.

We were pleased to hear from Brian Rice, one of our promising junior members, who is now with the Training Battalion R.A.S.C. and he says that he hopes to be able to turn out for the club during the present cross-country season.
Knights, a new member, ran well and we were pleased to see Brian Rice able to obtain leave from his unit.

Mike Stearman was our first man home in 6th place, then came Brian Trower 12th, Don McLean 14th, and Brian Rice 21st. Both Trower and MacLean are in the Forces, while Rice is at Cambridge University, and J.

Brian Rice, who is at Cambridge University, was reserve in the 4 x 880 for the Inter-Varsity Relays in December last, and Alan Sexton ran for Cambridge in the 4 x 110 yds., 4 x 220 yds., and the 4 x 440 yds., and led his team to victory in the latter event.
